payload.claim: Structural MRI, serum tau/GFAP, and monocyte transcriptomics are combined so that convergent signals jointly support the accelerated-aging conclusion.
The authors withhold a single-modality claim, demanding agreement across imaging, blood biomarkers, and transcriptomics before asserting accelerated brain aging.
A brain-age estimator yields the corrected brain-age gap (+6.5 years) that is the study's primary structural readout.
Serum brain-derived tau and GFAP are measured as peripheral biomarkers and found elevated in RA, indexing neural injury.
The reported metric is explicitly a corrected brain-age gap, applying the standard correction for the known age-dependent estimation bias before inference.
